structured_output.summary: Date.parse in parse.rs: ToString runs first with `?`, then the ISO path (existing helper date::parse_iso), then an implementation-specific fallback for the toString and toUTCString formats, then NaN. The fallback is permitted by the spec's implementation-defined clause. Month and weekday tables are format vocabulary, not test-shaped. Field ranges, the GMT±HHMM offset sign, the local-versus-UTC handling and time_clip all look correct. Only parse.rs changes. The lint flag on the skipped weekday is acceptable: the weekday is informative only and the fallback is implementation-specific.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Nothing blocking. Optional cleanups: (1) The comment above the `date::parse_iso(...)` call says non-conforming strings "fall back to NaN", but they actually go through parse_date_string first; reword it. (2) The substitution of absent MM/DD/HH/mm/ss/sss and the local-vs-UTC rule for ISO strings are delegated to the pre-existing helper crate::support::date::parse_iso, which is not in this diff. Verify it implements those steps before relying on the ISO path. (3) parse_date_string accepts out-of-month days such as "Feb 31" by rolling over through make_day; this is implementation-specific and not a defect, but it is a deliberate leniency.
